parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime for a visiting trans adult or family. No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented police targeting of trans people, and no documented border, custody or facility rules affecting visitors. Hate-crime penalties cover gender identity (2019), and gender identity is protected in services and goods (2015), though implementation is inconsistent. The state prosecuted an official for calling for LGBTQ beheadings. Against this, hostile political speech, death threats and marches held under threats are documented, and reporting is low. Traveller-facing exposure at borders, custody and care is undocumented, which is treated as an open question rather than safety. Resident-only gaps (recognition by court route, marriage, blood donation) are climate signals, not visitor exposure. Rated in the Reduced Risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: Not sourced: no material on how foreign documents with changed gender markers are read at entry, or on marker flagging.
entry_documents.protection: No documented entry restriction or denial aimed at trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign home-passport marker is the operative document; the resident court route is not the visitor's exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not sourced: no evidence on placement or treatment of trans people in police or immigration custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Police acted against an official who incited violence against LGBTQ people (2019), a sign that state actors face consequences.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody placement by birth sex is unknown, so the traveller's worst-case custody exposure stays open.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented facility-access restriction, bathroom rule or ban on trans visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented exclusion rule; anti-discrimination law covers goods and services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Enforcement of the 2015 law is documented as inconsistent, so a service refusal may be hard to remedy.

care_services.exposure: No source documents care access for short-term visitors; hormonal support runs through residents' NGO and ministry cooperation.
care_services.protection: An LGBTQI+ NGO offers reproductive and sexual health services and free HIV testing and PrEP (from 2024).
care_services.interaction: The NGO's services may be reachable by visitors, but eligibility is undocumented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Politicians' hate speech is common during civil-code debates; an artist received death threats; 2019 march held under multiple threats.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No criminalisation of trans identity or expression is documented; hate-crime penalties cover gender identity since 2019.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile political framing raises social hostility, but the state responded to one incitement case.

minors_guardians.exposure: A 2015 survey found over 97% unwilling to accept a child who came out as lesbian or gay; this concerns LGBTQ people broadly and is dated.
minors_guardians.protection: Age of consent is equal at 14 regardless of gender or orientation (2004), so no sexuality-based disparity applies to minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family-level friction is a local-sphere concern and is weakly relevant to visitors; no traveller-facing minors rule is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 10 bias crimes against LGBTQ people reported to police in 2019 and 13 only to NGOs; no trans-specific violence figure with a denominator.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime penalties cover gender identity; the capital's Pride has run since 2016 without documented violent incident, and the 2019 march passed without incident.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Under-reporting limits the evidence; the background trans-specific violence rate is unknowable.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gender-marker recognition runs case by case through courts; the ruling is not treated as precedent; administrative route status is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have ruled for a trans applicant without medical proof; anti-discrimination law has statutory coverage.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Resident-facing gaps are climate signals only; open questions remain on whether visitors face document scrutiny.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in form: national equality law covers gender identity and remedies work in some cases. This case is lower because the dossier shows no documented traveller-facing incident, no complaint outcomes, and weaker documented enforcement of the 2015 law. Documented political hate speech and threats to events are a further negative.

Lower-tier comparison: 0.55-B documents border secondary screening and denial of entry for visitors, which this dossier does not. This case is higher because no visitor-facing exclusion or detention pattern is recorded, though the entry and custody questions remain open.

Higher-tier comparison: 0.75-C has documented respectful border training, written reasons and compensation for unlawful holding. This dossier lacks any documented border protection, so it sits lower. It is still above a documented-hostility case because no visitor-facing harm is recorded.

parsed.synthesis: Documented positives (equal-age law, gender identity in hate-crime and anti-discrimination law, state prosecution of incitement, visible Pride operating) outweigh the documented negatives (political hate speech, death threats, low reporting, inconsistent enforcement). Traveller-facing exposures at borders, custody, facilities and care are not documented, so they cannot be credited as safe and are treated as open questions. Resident-facing gaps (court-only recognition, marriage, blood donation) are climate signals and do not drive the visitor rating. The result sits in the Reduced Risk band, lower than documented-protection jurisdictions because of the unresolved entry and custody questions and the documented political hostility.
